title: FAA Part 107 registration and Remote ID practice questions
description: Free practice questions on small drone registration (14 CFR Part 48) and Remote ID (Part 89). Every answer is explained and linked to its section.

questions.question: Under 48.15(b), an aircraft operated exclusively in compliance with 49 U.S.C. 44809 meets the registration requirement without Part 48 registration if it weighs how much on takeoff?

options.A: 0.55 pounds or less, including everything that is on board or otherwise attached to the aircraft
options.B: Less than 55 pounds, including everything that is on board or otherwise attached to the aircraft
options.C: 0.55 pounds or less, counting only the airframe and battery
options.D: 2 pounds or less, including everything that is on board or otherwise attached to the aircraft

questions.explanation: 48.15(b) covers an aircraft "operated exclusively in compliance with 49 U.S.C. 44809" that "weighs 0.55 pounds or less on takeoff, including everything that is on board or otherwise attached to the aircraft".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 48.15, Requirement to register (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The aircraft is operated exclusively in compliance with 49 U.S.C. 44809 and weighs 0.55 pounds or less on takeoff, including everything that is on board or otherwise attached to the aircraft

questions.question: Which of these is one of the three criteria in 48.15 that allows a small unmanned aircraft eligible for registration to be operated?

options.A: The aircraft is flown only over property owned by the remote pilot
options.B: The aircraft is operated under a certificate of waiver issued under Part 107
options.C: The aircraft is an aircraft of the Armed Forces of the United States
options.D: The aircraft weighs less than 55 pounds on takeoff

questions.explanation: 48.15 lists registration and marking under Part 48, the 0.55-pound limited recreational case, and (c): "The aircraft is an aircraft of the Armed Forces of the United States."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 48.15, Requirement to register (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The aircraft is an aircraft of the Armed Forces of the United States.

questions.question: How does 48.1(c) require a small unmanned aircraft intended to be operated outside the territorial airspace of the United States to be registered?

options.A: Under Part 48 only, with the registration number marked on an external surface
options.B: Under the laws of the country where it will be operated, with no U.S. registration
options.C: By filing a notice of identification under 89.130
options.D: Under subparts A and B of Part 47, with the identification and marking requirements of subparts A and C of Part 45

questions.explanation: 48.1(c) says such aircraft "must be registered in accordance with subparts A and B of part 47 and satisfy the identification and registration marking requirements of subparts A and C of part 45."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 48.1, Applicability (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Small unmanned aircraft intended to be operated outside of the territorial airspace of the United States, or registered through a trust or voting trust, must be registered in accordance with subparts A and B of part 47

questions.question: Under 48.25(b), who must register a small unmanned aircraft whose owner is less than 13 years of age?

options.A: The owner, using the owner's legal name
options.B: A person who is at least 13 years of age
options.C: A parent or legal guardian who holds a remote pilot certificate
options.D: The retailer that sold the aircraft

questions.explanation: 48.25(b): "If the owner is less than 13 years of age, then the small unmanned aircraft must be registered by a person who is at least 13 years of age."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 48.25, Applicants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: If the owner is less than 13 years of age, then the small unmanned aircraft must be registered by a person who is at least 13 years of age.

questions.question: According to 48.25(c), what is registration not evidence of in a proceeding in which ownership of an unmanned aircraft by a particular person is in issue?

options.A: Remote pilot certification
options.B: Aircraft ownership
options.C: Airworthiness of the aircraft
options.D: Compliance with Remote ID

questions.explanation: 48.25(c): "registration is not evidence of aircraft ownership in any proceeding in which ownership of an unmanned aircraft by a particular person is in issue."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 48.25, Applicants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: registration is not evidence of aircraft ownership in any proceeding in which ownership of an unmanned aircraft by a particular person is in issue.

questions.question: Which situation makes a small unmanned aircraft registration invalid under 48.120?

options.A: The applicant registers on behalf of an owner who is under 13 years of age
options.B: The applicant uses the web-based small unmanned aircraft registration system
options.C: The aircraft is later flown in limited recreational operations
options.D: The aircraft is registered in a foreign country at the time the registration is made

questions.explanation: 48.120 says registration is invalid if, at the time it is made, "The aircraft is registered in a foreign country"; registering for an owner under 13 is an express exception in 48.120(b).

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 48.120, Invalid registration (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The registration of a small unmanned aircraft is invalid if, at the time it is made— (a) The aircraft is registered in a foreign country;

questions.question: What expiration period does 48.100(c) set for a Certificate of Aircraft Registration that is not renewed?

options.A: 3 years after the date of issue
options.B: 1 year after the date of issue
options.C: 5 years after the date of issue
options.D: It does not expire while the owner keeps the aircraft

questions.explanation: 48.100(c): a certificate "expires 3 years after the date of issue unless it is renewed."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 48.100, Registration: Small unmanned aircraft operated for any purpose other than exclusively limited recreational operations (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: A Certificate of Aircraft registration issued under this part expires 3 years after the date of issue unless it is renewed.

questions.question: What window does 48.100(c)(1) set for the verification that renews a Certificate of Aircraft Registration?

options.A: Only during the calendar month in which the certificate expires
options.B: Any time within the 30 days after the certificate expires
options.C: Any time within the six months preceding the month in which the certificate expires
options.D: Any time within the 12 months after the month in which the certificate expires

questions.explanation: 48.100(c)(1): "The verification may take place at any time within the six months preceding the month in which the Certificate of Aircraft registration expires."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 48.100, Registration: Small unmanned aircraft operated for any purpose other than exclusively limited recreational operations (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The verification may take place at any time within the six months preceding the month in which the Certificate of Aircraft registration expires.

questions.question: Under 48.105(a), what does a Certificate of Aircraft Registration for small unmanned aircraft operated exclusively in compliance with 49 U.S.C. 44809 cover?

options.A: Only the one aircraft identified by serial number on the application
options.B: Up to three aircraft owned by the individual
options.C: All the small unmanned aircraft used exclusively for those operations owned by the individual identified on the application
options.D: All aircraft flown by any member of the applicant's household

questions.explanation: 48.105(a): the certificate "constitutes registration for all the small unmanned aircraft used exclusively for operations in compliance with 49 U.S.C. 44809 owned by the individual identified on the application."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 48.105, Registration: Small unmanned aircraft intended exclusively for limited recreational operations (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: constitutes registration for all the small unmanned aircraft used exclusively for operations in compliance with 49 U.S.C. 44809 owned by the individual identified on the application.

questions.question: What deadline does 48.115(b) set for the holder to update registration information after a change in the information provided under 48.110?

options.A: 30 days
options.B: 14 calendar days
options.C: 60 days
options.D: At the next renewal

questions.explanation: 48.115(b): the holder "must update the information using the web-based small unmanned aircraft registration system within 14 calendar days" of a change or a required cancellation.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 48.115, Requirement to maintain current information (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: must update the information using the web-based small unmanned aircraft registration system within 14 calendar days of the following

questions.question: Where does 48.205(c) require the unique identifier to be legibly displayed?

options.A: Inside the battery compartment
options.B: On the control station or remote controller
options.C: On the Certificate of Aircraft Registration only
options.D: On an external surface of the small unmanned aircraft

questions.explanation: 48.205(c): "The unique identifier must be legibly displayed on an external surface of the small unmanned aircraft."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 48.205, Display and location of unique identifier (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The unique identifier must be legibly displayed on an external surface of the small unmanned aircraft.

questions.question: Besides the registration number issued by the Registry, what does 48.200(b) allow as a unique identifier?

options.A: If authorized by the Administrator, the small unmanned aircraft serial number provided with the registration application
options.B: The remote pilot certificate number of the person who usually flies the aircraft
options.C: The owner's telephone number
options.D: The radio equipment authorization number on the aircraft's label

questions.explanation: 48.200(b)(2) allows, "If authorized by the Administrator, the small unmanned aircraft serial number provided with the application for Certificate of Aircraft Registration under § 48.110(a)."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 48.200, General (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: If authorized by the Administrator, the small unmanned aircraft serial number provided with the application for Certificate of Aircraft Registration under § 48.110(a).

questions.question: After what date does 89.105 bar operating an unmanned aircraft within U.S. airspace unless the operation meets 89.110 or 89.115 (except as otherwise authorized or as provided in 89.120)?

options.A: January 15, 2021
options.B: September 16, 2023
options.C: December 21, 2015

questions.explanation: 89.105: "after September 16, 2023, no person may operate an unmanned aircraft within the airspace of the United States unless the operation meets the requirements of § 89.110 or § 89.115."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 89.105, Remote identification requirement (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: after September 16, 2023, no person may operate an unmanned aircraft within the airspace of the United States unless the operation meets the requirements of § 89.110 or § 89.115.

questions.question: What does 89.125 state about ADS-B Out equipment?

options.A: It may replace a remote identification broadcast module if it is FAA-approved
options.B: It satisfies Remote ID only inside an FAA-recognized identification area
options.C: It must be installed on every standard remote identification unmanned aircraft
options.D: It cannot be used to comply with the remote identification requirements of Part 89

questions.explanation: 89.125: "Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) Out equipment cannot be used to comply with the remote identification requirements of this part."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 89.125, Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) Out prohibition (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) Out equipment cannot be used to comply with the remote identification requirements of this part.

questions.question: Under 89.110(a)(2), what must the person manipulating the flight controls do if a standard remote identification unmanned aircraft is no longer broadcasting the 89.305 message elements?

options.A: Land the unmanned aircraft as soon as practicable
options.B: Finish the planned flight and repair the equipment before the next flight
options.C: Continue the flight only within visual line of sight
options.D: Notify air traffic control and continue the flight

questions.explanation: 89.110(a)(2): the person manipulating the flight controls "must land the unmanned aircraft as soon as practicable" if the aircraft "is no longer broadcasting the message elements of § 89.305."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 89.110, Operation of standard remote identification unmanned aircraft (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The person manipulating the flight controls of the unmanned aircraft system must land the unmanned aircraft as soon as practicable if the standard remote identification unmanned aircraft is no longer broadcasting the message elements of § 89.305.

questions.question: Under 89.110(b)(4), what must the Certificate of Aircraft Registration of a standard remote identification unmanned aircraft include, unless that number is provided to the FAA in a notice of identification under 89.130 before the operation?

options.A: The remote pilot certificate number of the person manipulating the flight controls
options.B: The date of the aircraft's last maintenance check
options.C: The serial number of the unmanned aircraft
options.D: The location of the operator's usual take-off site

questions.explanation: 89.110(b)(4): the certificate "must include the serial number of the unmanned aircraft", or the serial number "must be provided to the FAA in a notice of identification pursuant to § 89.130 prior to the operation."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 89.110, Operation of standard remote identification unmanned aircraft (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The Certificate of Aircraft Registration of the unmanned aircraft used in the operation must include the serial number of the unmanned aircraft

questions.question: What does 89.115(a)(2)(ii) require of the person manipulating the flight controls when operating with a remote identification broadcast module?

options.A: Staying within 400 feet of the take-off location
options.B: Being able to see the unmanned aircraft at all times throughout the operation
options.C: Keeping the module's serial number displayed on the control station
options.D: Carrying a printed copy of the declaration of compliance

questions.explanation: 89.115(a)(2)(ii): the person manipulating the flight controls "must be able to see the unmanned aircraft at all times throughout the operation."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 89.115, Alternative remote identification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The person manipulating the flight controls of the unmanned aircraft system must be able to see the unmanned aircraft at all times throughout the operation.

questions.question: Which location does 89.315 require a remote identification broadcast module to be capable of broadcasting, along with the unmanned aircraft's own position?

options.A: The latitude and longitude of the nearest airport
options.B: The owner's registered physical address
options.C: The latitude and longitude of the control station
options.D: The latitude, longitude and geometric altitude of the take-off location of the unmanned aircraft

questions.explanation: 89.315 lists "An indication of the latitude and longitude of the take-off location of the unmanned aircraft" and "An indication of the geometric altitude of the take-off location of the unmanned aircraft"; the control station position is in the 89.305 list for standard remote ID aircraft.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 89.315, Minimum message elements broadcast by remote identification broadcast modules (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (e) An indication of the latitude and longitude of the take-off location of the unmanned aircraft. (f) An indication of the geometric altitude of the take-off location of the unmanned aircraft.

questions.question: Which of these is eligible under 89.205 to apply for the establishment of an FAA-recognized identification area?

options.A: Any individual who holds a remote pilot certificate
options.B: A manufacturer of remote identification broadcast modules
options.C: An educational institution, such as a trade school or university
options.D: A commercial drone service company

questions.explanation: 89.205 says "Only the following persons are eligible": "A community-based organization recognized by the Administrator" and "An educational institution, including primary and secondary educational institutions, trade schools, colleges, and universities."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 89.205, Eligibility (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: An educational institution, including primary and secondary educational institutions, trade schools, colleges, and universities.

questions.question: Except as otherwise provided in subpart C of Part 89, how long does 89.225(a) say an FAA-recognized identification area is in effect?

options.A: 48 calendar months after the date the FAA approves the request
options.B: 12 calendar months after the date the FAA approves the request
options.C: 24 calendar months after the date the FAA approves the request
options.D: Indefinitely, until the FAA terminates it

questions.explanation: 89.225(a): an FAA-recognized identification area "will be in effect for 48 calendar months after the date the FAA approves the request for establishment of an FAA-recognized identification area."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 89.225, Duration of an FAA-recognized identification area (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: an FAA-recognized identification area will be in effect for 48 calendar months after the date the FAA approves the request for establishment of an FAA-recognized identification area.
